meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid civil-law system with statutory company, tax, administrative, and AML frameworks
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Cross-Strait Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement (ECFA), subject to its applicable scope and implementation status
Cross-Strait Agreement on Avoidance of Double Taxation and Enhancement of Tax Cooperation, signed in 2015; applicability and implementation must be confirmed for the relevant parties and transaction
Taiwan has separate tax agreements and investment arrangements with numerous jurisdictions; no assumption should be made that a PRC treaty applies in Taiwan
meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdictional_compatibility_warning: A Taiwan-incorporated company is not a PRC Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise. The proposed CN_WFOE_LTD structure must be legally reclassified as a Taiwan company limited by shares, Taiwan company limited by shares with foreign investment, or Taiwan branch of a foreign company. PRC WFOE statutes do not govern a Taiwan entity. A PRC-incorporated parent investing into Taiwan may also require separate PRC outbound-investment, foreign-exchange, and cross-Strait approvals or filings.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Taiwan Money Laundering Control Act, Articles 7 and 8; Taiwan Company Act, Article 22-1; Regulations Governing Anti-Money Laundering of Financial Institutions; Regulations Governing Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Terrorism Financing for Enterprises Handling Virtual Currency Platform or Trading Business, where applicable; Taiwan Company Act and Ministry of Economic Affairs rules governing company ownership, responsible persons, directors, managers, and actual controllers. Taiwan does not operate a fully public, general-purpose UBO register equivalent to a public beneficial-ownership database.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_identification_rule: The beneficial owner is generally the natural person ultimately owning or controlling, directly or indirectly, 25 percent or more of the equity or voting rights, or otherwise exercising ultimate effective control. If no natural person can be identified under ownership or control tests, the senior managing official is used as the fallback identification person. Financial institutions may apply stricter control and verification standards.

Certified constitutional documents and current good-standing or incumbency evidence for each corporate shareholder
Complete ownership chart tracing through all intermediate entities to natural persons
Natural-person identity, nationality, residential address, date of birth, tax identification details where requested, and control rationale
Director, manager, authorized representative, protector, settlor, trustee, beneficiary, and equivalent control-person information for trusts, foundations, partnerships, and nominee structures

ubo_and_aml_profiling.document_freshness_rule: Taiwan company-registration law does not impose one universal 90-day validity period for every foreign document. The 90-day period is a conservative operational standard commonly imposed by banks, professional intermediaries, and reviewing authorities. The receiving institution's current checklist controls.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Screen all natural persons and entities before engagement, incorporation, capital remittance, banking, payment processing, and material ownership changes against United Nations Security Council sanctions, Taiwan sanctions and terrorism-financing lists, PRC sanctions and counter-sanctions lists where relevant, United States OFAC lists where a US nexus exists, EU and UK lists where relevant, and applicable domestic law-enforcement or regulatory notices. Conduct PEP, family-member, and known-close-associate screening; obtain source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence for PEPs, sanctioned-country exposure, opaque structures, nominee arrangements, adverse media, unusual payment flows, and high-risk intermediaries. Apply enhanced due diligence and senior approval for matches or elevated risk. Do not treat a screening hit as conclusive without identity-resolution analysis.

Nominee shareholder, bearer-like control arrangement, trust, foundation, or unexplained layered ownership
Inconsistent ownership information across registry, tax, banking, and corporate documents
Payments involving high-risk jurisdictions, mixers, virtual assets, or unrelated third parties
PEP, sanctions, terrorism-financing, export-control, corruption, or serious adverse-media indicators

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce, Company Name and Business Scope Pre-check system, accessed through the MOEA one-stop company and business registration services portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.competent_registry_authority: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce, with local government authority involvement where the relevant registration type requires it
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered Chinese company name must use permitted Traditional Chinese characters and comply with Taiwan company-naming rules. An English name may be recorded or used commercially but does not replace the statutory Chinese name. Transliteration is not a substitute for an approved Chinese name. The proposed business scope must correspond to permitted business items and any required special licensing.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words implying government, ministry, public authority, central bank, diplomatic status, or official institutional status without authorization

Terms implying banking, finance, securities, insurance, trust, investment, telecommunications, healthcare, education, travel, legal services, or other regulated activities without the relevant approval
Words likely to create confusion with an existing company, trademark, government body, public-interest institution, or famous enterprise
National, international, central, official, academy, association, chamber, foundation, or equivalent sensitive terms where prior approval or substantiation is required
Obscene, deceptive, discriminatory, public-order, or misleading terms
Terms suggesting a business activity outside the approved scope or requiring a licence not held by the applicant
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.name_reservation_rule: Taiwan company-name and business-scope pre-check approval is generally valid for six months, subject to the applicable registration rules and current MOEA system instructions. The six-month period is not the 30-day period stated in the generic schema.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Obtain the written or electronic rejection reason and identify whether the issue is similarity, prohibited terminology, incomplete Chinese wording, business-scope mismatch, or missing sector approval. Submit an amended name through the MOEA pre-check system, or file the available administrative review, correction, or objection request with the issuing authority within the stated deadline. Provide evidence of distinctiveness, applicant identity, corporate relationship, trademark rights, authorization for sensitive terminology, and the proposed business scope. If the authority maintains the rejection, file an administrative appeal under the Administrative Appeal Act with the competent superior authority and preserve all filing receipts. Judicial administrative litigation may be considered after exhaustion or where legally available. A rejected name should not be used in contracts, invoices, bank applications, or public marketing.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.trademark_clearance_requirement: Company-name approval does not establish trademark ownership or freedom to operate. Conduct separate searches in the Taiwan Intellectual Property Office trademark database and relevant international databases for the Chinese name, English name, logo, product names, and keycap designs.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.statutory_basis: Taiwan Company Act provisions requiring a company to have a registered office and register its principal business address, together with business-registration, tax-registration, zoning, fire-safety, and sector-specific requirements applicable to the actual premises and activities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office may be accepted for a holding, consulting, or administrative company if the address owner consents, the premises satisfy registration and zoning requirements, mail and official notices can be received, and the company does not misrepresent its operations. It is high risk for a manufacturing, injection-molding, product-development, warehousing, or fulfilment business. A registered office cannot substitute for legally compliant production, storage, labour-safety, environmental, fire-safety, import, export, or product-compliance premises.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.industry_specific_substance_assessment: Double-shot PBT plastic injection of novelty keyboard keycaps is generally not a separately licensed business activity solely by virtue of the product description, but the actual factory may require factory registration, land-use compatibility, building and fire approvals, occupational-safety controls, environmental permits, waste-management compliance, and customs or product-safety registrations depending on scale, location, machinery, emissions, and materials.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No reliable public statistical rate is published. Indicative risk assessment: low to moderate during ordinary incorporation if the registered address is conventional and documents are consistent; moderate to high for a manufacturing address, factory registration, tax audit, environmental or fire review, suspicious ownership, inconsistent business scope, or payment-service-provider onboarding. Treat the probability of a targeted inspection or documentary verification during the first operating cycle as materially higher than for a passive office company; do not rely on an unstaffed virtual office.
substance_requirements: Real personnel or outsourced operational capability appropriate to the stated business model
Books, invoices, contracts, inventory, manufacturing or supplier records, and bank activity consistent with the registered business
Evidence of management decision-making and control in Taiwan where Taiwan tax residence or local substance is claimed
Separate documentation for third-party manufacturing, warehousing, logistics, Shopify Payments, Stripe, and customer-service functions
Transfer-pricing support for transactions with the PRC parent or related parties

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Act of the Republic of China (Taiwan), Articles 1-20 (Incorporation), 128-156 (Share Capital), 192-206 (Directors and Board Meetings), 208-210 (Officers), and 387 (Registration)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commerce, Company Registration Section
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation and Application for Company Registration (Form 1)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a WFOE under the Company Act; however, the capital must be reasonably sufficient to cover initial operating expenses and must be remitted from abroad via foreign exchange settlement. The capital is not required to be placed in a blocked escrow account, but the remittance must be evidenced by a bank certificate for registration purposes.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED (the 'Company'), HELD ON [DATE] AT [TIME] AT THE REGISTERED OFFICE OF THE COMPANY.

1. SUBSCRIPTION OF SHARE CAPITAL
RESOLVED, that the Company hereby subscribes to the entire authorized share capital of [amount] New Taiwan Dollars (NT$[amount]), divided into [number] shares of NT$[par value] each, and that the initial shareholders, as listed in the Articles of Incorporation, have each subscribed to the number of shares set opposite their respective names. The Board acknowledges receipt of the capital contribution in full, as evidenced by the bank certificate of deposit issued by [Bank Name], and directs the Company Secretary to file the necessary capital verification documents with the Ministry of Economic Affairs.

2. ADOPTION OF REGISTERED OFFICE

3. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS

- [Name] as Chairperson of the Board and Managing Director;

- [Name] as Chief Financial Officer and Principal Accounting Officer.
The Board confirms that each appointee has consented to serve and possesses the requisite qualifications under the Company Act and applicable regulations.

4. BANKING AUTHORIZATION

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) – Company Name Reservation Online System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application via the MOEA's online portal, providing the proposed English and Chinese company names, the intended business scope (ISIC 3240 – Manufacture of musical instruments, but specifically for custom mechanical keyboard caps), and the proposed registered office address. The name must not conflict with existing registered entities or trademarks. The application must be signed by the proposed incorporator or a notarized power of attorney if filed by an agent. Upon approval, the name reservation is valid for six months. Ensure that the name includes the term 'Limited' or 'Co., Ltd.' to denote limited liability.
required_dossiers: Copy of the applicant's passport or ID
Power of attorney (if filed by an agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity or prohibited terms, file a revised application with a new name within 5 business days. If the rejection is based on trademark conflict, provide evidence of consent from the trademark owner or amend the name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (for notarization) and MOEA (for approval of articles)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed corporate attorney to draft the Articles of Incorporation in accordance with the Company Act. The articles must include the company name, business scope, registered office address, share capital structure, classes of shares, rights of shareholders, board composition, and quorum requirements. After drafting, the Articles must be signed by all initial shareholders and directors. The signatures must be notarized by a Taiwan notary public, who will verify the identity and capacity of the signatories. The notarized Articles are then submitted to the MOEA for approval as part of the incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Shareholders' identification documents (passports or national IDs)
Registered office lease or ownership proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MOEA returns the Articles for corrections, address the specific deficiencies within 10 business days. Common issues include missing mandatory clauses or inconsistent capital amounts. Re-notarization may be required if changes are substantive.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application to MOEA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) – Department of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the complete incorporation application package with the MOEA, including the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the name reservation certificate, the capital verification certificate from a bank, and the registration fee payment. The application must be submitted online or in person. The MOEA will review the documents for compliance with the Company Act and issue the Company Registration Certificate upon approval. This certificate is the legal proof of incorporation. After issuance, the company must obtain a company seal and register for tax identification number (TIN) with the National Taxation Bureau.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MOEA issues a query or suspension, respond within 15 days with clarifications or additional documents. Common queries include discrepancies in capital remittance or missing signatures. If the application is rejected, re-file after correcting the issues; the name reservation may be extended if still valid.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Registrations and Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau (TIN), Local Labor Department, and Commercial Bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Company Registration Certificate, the company must complete the following: (1) Register for a Tax Identification Number (TIN) with the National Taxation Bureau within 15 days; (2) Register as an employer with the local labor department for social insurance and labor pension; (3) Open a corporate bank account with a commercial bank, presenting the Company Registration Certificate, the TIN certificate, the Articles of Incorporation, and the board resolution authorizing signatories. The bank will conduct a KYC review and may require the physical presence of the authorized signatories.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the account opening due to incomplete documentation, provide the missing items within 5 business days. If the tax bureau delays TIN issuance, follow up with the assigned officer; escalate to the branch chief if necessary. For labor registration, ensure all employee data is accurate to avoid penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs – Industrial Development Bureau (IDB) and Local Municipal Government – Department of Economic Development
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Factory Registration Certificate (under the Factory Management Act)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – Environmental Impact Assessment Report (for manufacturing facilities with annual production capacity exceeding 1,000 metric tons of plastic products, or with significant wastewater discharge)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: pH 6-9, COD ≤ 100 mg/L, BOD ≤ 30 mg/L, SS ≤ 30 mg/L; VOCs: ≤ 0.6 kg/hr per emission source; Hazardous waste: must be stored in sealed containers and disposed of by licensed contractors; compliance with Taiwan's Air Pollution Control Act and Water Pollution Control Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certification from the local Fire Department (required for all manufacturing premises, including fire extinguishers, sprinklers, and emergency exits); Structural Load Inspection certificate from the local Construction Management Office; Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) approval for workplace safety, including machine guarding and personal protective equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); online portal is the State Taxation Administration Electronic Tax Bureau at https://etax.chinatax.gov.cn
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the China WFOE, the initial step is incorporation with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), which issues the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) that serves as the national taxpayer identification number. Within 30 calendar days of the business license issuance, the WFOE must complete tax registration with the local STA office through the Electronic Tax Bureau, submitting the business license, articles of association, legal representative identification, registered address proof, bank information, and required shareholder documentation. The electronic registration automatically enrols the entity for corporate income tax, value added tax, stamp tax, and social insurance levies. After registration, the entity must enrol either as a small-scale VAT taxpayer or as a general VAT taxpayer through the VAT Invoice Management System; the general taxpayer election is mandatory once annual taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000. In the case of a foreign non-resident investor or cross-border e-commerce platform service provider operating without a permanent establishment in China, the foreign entity must separately obtain a Chinese taxpayer identification number through the non-resident enterprise registration module of the Electronic Tax Bureau, using its home-jurisdiction tax residence certificate and appointing a China withholding agent where necessary.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The PRC tax system does not provide a US-style check-the-box entity classification election, and the China WFOE is mandatorily treated as a resident enterprise subject to entity-level corporate income tax on worldwide income. Available administrative elections are confined to VAT small-scale versus general taxpayer status and the reduced corporate income tax treatment for qualified small and low-profit enterprises; these are not hybrid mismatch or pass-through check-the-box elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) of the People's Republic of China, administered by the State Taxation Administration
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: All enterprises must complete VAT registration upon incorporation; no turnover-based exemption exists. The mandatory threshold for classification as a general VAT taxpayer is annual taxable turnover of RMB 5,000,000. Below this threshold, the enterprise qualifies as a small-scale taxpayer and may apply a reduced levy rate (typically 1% to 3%) unless it voluntarily elects general taxpayer status.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China mandates real-time invoice data transmission through the State Taxation Administration's VAT Invoice Management System and the nationwide Digital Electronic Invoice (fully digitalised e-invoice) platform. All VAT invoices, including special VAT invoices, must be generated through STA-approved fiscal infrastructure and carry a unique encrypted invoice code assigned by the national e-invoice clearance database. E-invoices are delivered in structured data format through API integration with the taxpayer's accounting or e-commerce system; issuance, cancellation, and red-document reversal are processed online with mandatory filing of each invoice before legal circulation. The use of tax-controlling encrypted stamps and the real-time reporting of sales data constitute the anti-fraud clearance mandate.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The export of custom mechanical keyboard keycaps from the PRC customs territory qualifies for zero-rating (exemption and credit/refund) provided the exporter is a VAT general taxpayer, is the declared consignor under the customs export declaration, the goods are physically exported via a PRC customs port, the sale is supported by genuine cross-border commercial documentation, export proceeds are repatriated to China and substantiated through the banking system, and the export-tag VAT invoice has been issued and filed with the STA. Qualifying sales through cross-border e-commerce platforms to overseas consumers using declared trade data are eligible under the integrated cross-border e-commerce retail export policy.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or bank-issued export proceeds receipt under SAFE
Export Goods Tax Rebate declaration in the Electronic Tax Bureau
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange perform cross-referenced scrutiny of export declarations, transport documents, payment rails, and bank foreign-exchange receipts. If zero-rated export VAT treatment is claimed without complete physical exportation, without the required customs clearance documents, or without verified repatriation of the export proceeds within the 180-day statutory window, the zero-rating is denied, the VAT refund is clawed back with retrospective interest, and a penalty ranging from 50% to 500% of the tax amount evaded is imposed. Deliberate fraudulent export-rebate schemes are referred for criminal investigation under the Criminal Law, with possible imprisonment, fines, forfeiture, and downgrading of the taxpayer's credit status, which may trigger interruption of VAT e-invoice issuance and export declaration privileges.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBoC) and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Republic of China
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Under the PBoC and SAFE framework, RMB is conditionally convertible: current account transactions, including trade in goods and reasonable service payments, are freely convertible and require real-trade supporting documentation. Capital account transactions, including inbound direct investment contributed by a Taiwan shareholder to a China WFOE, remain subject to SAFE registration, foreign exchange account controls, and post-verification settlement. A Taiwan-funded WFOE may receive capital contributions in a foreign currency only after completing the Foreign-Exchange Business Registration for direct investment; once credited, the capital funds may be settled into RMB only against verified operating use such as the purchase of PBT resin, molds, or manufacturing equipment. Profit remittance to the Taiwan shareholder is permitted after annual audit, corporate income tax filing, and provision of a board resolution, audited financials, and tax clearance; no separate repatriation tax is imposed, but the outbound remittance is executed through a domestic bank and may be delayed or rejected if the tax certificate or capital verification files are incomplete. The convertibility risk is therefore concentrated in the capital account and profit repatriation process rather than in ordinary trade settlement, but the WFOE must maintain disciplined SAFE filing and documentation hygiene to keep the clearing rails open.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SAFE goods-trade administration, there is no mandatory percentage for conversion to CNY; export proceeds may be retained in a foreign exchange settlement account or sold to banks. However, all proceeds from the export of custom mechanical keyboard keycaps must be repatriated into China within 180 days after the export customs declaration, unless the WFOE obtains SAFE approval for offshore retention under the pilot programme. After repatriation, the WFOE must complete trade-in-flow verification through the Digital Foreign Exchange Management Platform and may keep funds in foreign currency or settle them to RMB at a negotiated spot or forward rate. Any excess unverified inflow may be treated as an export under-declaration or trade-based money laundering trigger, so the statutory 180-day timeline and the 0% forced conversion ratio require active treasury controls.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Foreign Currency Capital Account)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational RMB Account and Foreign Currency Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account and Trade Settlement Account
Operational RMB Account with Trade Disbursement Modules

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Airwallex, or Stripe Treasury generally cannot serve as the primary banking rail for a China WFOE because they lack a PBoC-licensed domestic payment institution license and cannot open local settlement accounts for the entity. They may only be used as supplementary collection channels for Shopify and Stripe card receipts through licensed cross-border payment processors, and all funds must still be repatriated into a domestic tier-1 bank through SAFE-compliant channels. Legal viability as a primary treasury rail is Low; viability as a limited e-commerce collection front-end is Conditional Medium, and the WFOE should never route capital injection or statutory tax payments through an offshore EMI.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: PBoC and tier-1 commercial bank KYC rules do not require the Taiwan statutory director to appear physically in every case, but the bank compliance committee generally mandates an in-person interview with the legal representative or a senior authorised representative. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted for initial WFOE account activation. The Taiwan shareholder may execute a notarised power of attorney, and a locally appointed representative or operator must appear in branch with the original corporate seals, notarised shareholder registration documents, the China WFOE business licence, SAFE FDI registration, and shareholder identification. Some tier-1 banks also require a board resolution and a physical site visit to the keycap manufacturing facility before activating high-volume outbound trade payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership opacity where the Taiwan shareholder is a holding vehicle, or where a nominee local representative is used to manage the WFOE.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full group structure chart, certificates of incorporation and articles of association for all intermediate entities, register of directors and shareholders, notarised ultimate beneficial owner declaration, passport copies of all natural persons holding more than 10%, and a professional legal reference from a Taiwan licensed attorney explaining the source of capital and the commercial purpose of the holding chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the capital injection narrative and the stated business scope of manufacturing custom mechanical keyboard keycaps, triggering suspicion of round-tripping, disguised cross-border loans, or shell company structuring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board minutes approving the capital injection, signed investment contract, SAFE Foreign-Exchange Business Registration certificate, CPA capital verification report, pro-forma invoices for production equipment and PBT resin, supply agreements with resin vendors, and verified e-commerce end-customer purchase orders from Shopify and Stripe channels.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media, sanctions list, or PEP screening hits on the Taiwan shareholder, directors, or on the trademark and branding associated with the novelty keycap product line.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Negative-news explanation memo, PEP and sanctions red-flag clearance from a reputable KYC screening database, registered trademark certificates, transaction rationale for high-value custom keycap sets, evidence of physical manufacturing operations including factory lease agreement, utility bills, equipment purchase invoices, and payroll records for local staff.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unsupported high-volume outbound trade payments to overseas suppliers or contract manufacturers, which may be perceived as trade-based money laundering if the payment flow does not match physical goods movement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Per-transaction contract, pro-forma invoice, commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading or air waybill, customs export declaration, quality inspection report, payment schedule, and bank routing instructions consistent with the underlying shipment records and the keycap product description.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwan shareholder must route investment funds via SWIFT MT103 to the WFOE's Foreign Currency Capital Account at a tier-1 domestic commercial bank, using the remitter name exactly matching the SAFE FDI registration. The bank will require the SAFE business registration code, a detailed remittance purpose referencing direct investment, and an internal remittance instruction. The funds must be held in the capital escrow account until the bank validates the Foreign-Exchange Business Registration and the underlying investment contract. Once validated, the WFOE may apply for capital settlement into RMB against verified operating uses such as equipment import, raw material purchase, rent, and salaries. A CPA must issue a capital verification report within the statutory filing window, and the WFOE should retain the MT103 confirmation, SAFE registration certificate, board resolution, and bank settlement voucher for future profit repatriation and tax audits.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for raw material imports and overseas supplier payments should use SWIFT MT103 direct wires for standard purchase orders, commercial letters of credit for large-volume resin or mold purchases, and documentary collections such as D/P or D/A for lower-risk supplier relationships. All outbound current-account payments must be matched with contracts, invoices, customs declarations, and logistics documents; RMB cross-border payments can be cleared through CIPS, while USD, EUR, or TWD payments should use standard SWIFT rails. The WFOE should maintain a single domestic bank relationship for outbound disbursements to avoid fragmenting the audit trail, and should pre-notify the bank of any unusually large or repeated MT103 payment to a single supplier to prevent autonomous transaction freezes.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore CNY/USD deliverable FX forward contracts with a SAFE-licensed domestic bank under genuine trade or capital exposure
Onshore FX swaps for rolling near-term trade settlement and working capital needs
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for medium-term funding and capital exposure related to the WFOE
Structured options comprising forwards and limited-premium FX options subject to SAFE real-needs verification
Offshore CNH non-deliverable forwards are not permissible for an onshore WFOE; all hedging must be executed through onshore SAFE-regulated instruments with documented underlying exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax (CIT) Final Settlement Return (including appendix statements and audited financial statements)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) — competent in-charge tax bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before May 31 of the year following the reported tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of RMB 1,000–10,000 for late filing; daily surcharge of 0.05% on unpaid tax from the due date; serious violations may trigger compulsory enforcement and tax credit downgrade

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Information Report and Foreign Investment Information Report (incorporating UBO/actual controller confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System; information shared with Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from January 1 through June 30 for the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Listed in the Business Operation Exception List; fine up to RMB 10,000; if not remedied for three consecutive years, the enterprise is placed on the Serious Illegal and Untrustworthy List and may be administratively struck off (i.e., license revoked)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) Stock Ownership Register (Foreign Exchange annual data return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) via the Capital Project Information System (submitted through bank or directly)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from January 1 through June 30 for stock ownership data as at the end of the preceding year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to RMB 300,000 under the PRC Foreign Exchange Administration Regulations; possible suspension of foreign exchange business pending rectification

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No threshold exemption: every WFOE limited-liability company must have its annual financial statements audited by a licensed PRC CPA under Article 164 of the Company Law and Article 34 of the Foreign Investment Law
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (CAS) (converged with IFRS); eligible small/medium enterprises may adopt the Small Enterprise Accounting Standards (SME CAS)

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The ultimate beneficial owner (actual controller) must be confirmed in each annual information report; any equity transfer must be filed with SAMR for registration within 30 days of the change and publicly posted on NECIPS within 20 working days; failure to update UBO data constitutes a false filing under market regulation law
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Shareholders' and Board Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 – USD 1,200 per year (registered address / company secretarial agent in PRC tier-1 and tier-2 cities)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 700 – USD 3,000 per year (SME WFOE, depending on asset size, revenue volume and transaction complexity)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Taiwan operates a single-tier shareholder taxation system. No broad statutory tax holiday applies to ISIC 3240 precision plastic injection manufacturers. According to Taiwan Income Tax Act Art. 43-3 and related investment regulations, the only meaningful CIT reductions are: (a) R&D expense investment tax credit (ITC) of up to 15% of qualifying R&D costs against corporate tax liability; (b) ITC for qualifying automation/machinery used for double-shot PBT injection moulding under the industrial automation guidelines if elected and certified; (c) exemption or deferral reserved for certain qualifying strategic industries — not available for custom keycap manufacture. The headline 20% rate is imposed only on taxable income after the 10-year loss carryforward relief and the 12% Alternative Minimum Tax (AMT) floor. An additional 5% retained-earnings surtax applies on undistributed earnings exceeding a  20% sustainability threshold, at the discretion of the shareholder.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return, Form 15 (營利事業所得稅結算申報書, 申報書15類); filed electronically via the Ministry of Finance electronic filing platform '財政部電子申報繳稅服務網' (e-Gov Tax Filing) with the Taiwan National Taxation Bureau (NTB). The WFOE must also file the related-party disclosure schedule (附冊四: 關係人交易明細表) and the quarterly provisional tax return (暫繳申報書) on Form 15-A.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (mandatory finalization) with quarterly provisional tax remittances
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return: filed between 1 May and 31 May of the calendar year following the fiscal-year end (within five months after the close of the profit-seeking enterprise year). For an entity with a fiscal year commencing 1 January, the deadline is 31 May. Provisional quarterly prepayment: 1–30 September (for calendar-year entities) at 50% of the preceding year's assessed tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 01 – Operating Revenue Total (營業收入總額)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate gross sales and service revenue, including export sales of custom mechanical keyboard keycaps to related or third-party purchasers, before returns, discounts, and tax-exclusive treatment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Taiwan WFOE must include all revenue sourced in Taiwan, including cross-border B2B/B2C e-commerce shipments that originate from Taiwan. Revenue routed through overseas marketplaces (Shopify/Stripe settlements) remains fully taxable in Taiwan.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 04 – Net Operating Revenue (營業收入淨額)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue less sales returns (Box 02) and sales discounts/allowed rebates (Box 03). For custom injection-moulded keycaps, freight allowances and platform fees that are contractual revenue deductions must be carefully documented.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Sales returns from related-party distributors must be supported by reverse logistics customs declarations. The overseas parent cannot unilaterally retro-offset Taiwan revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Inventory cost of goods sold, mould tooling amortization, PBT resin consumption, direct labour, and manufacturing overhead. The WFOE must reconcile its cost ledger with the Customs export records for the period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany purchase of raw materials from the parent or its affiliates must be priced at arm's length or the cost inclusion will be re-characterised under Article 43-1.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net revenue minus operating costs. Any concessionary gross margin below the profit level indicator selected in the TP documentation (typically full cost plus or transactional net margin for manufacturing contract) constitutes a red flag.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Taiwan manufacturing WFOE may not lawfully earn a zero or de-minimis markup on keycap production; the NTB treats this as profit shifting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 07 – Operating Expenses and Losses (營業費用及損失)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Marketing, selling, general and administrative expenses. Includes platform commissions paid to Shopify Payments/Stripe, warehouse costs, and trade-related bank charges. Unsupported overseas head-office cost allocations are not deductible.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintenance management fees paid to the Chinese group must satisfy the TP regulations and substantiation standards; otherwise add-back plus penalty applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 08/Box 11 – Net Operating Profit and Annual Income (營業淨利 / 全年所得額)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Summation lines aggregating operating income with non-operating items (interest, foreign exchange gains, asset disposal profits). Foreign exchange volatility on US-denominated Shopify settlements must be booked under Taiwan IFRS.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-operating intercompany financing income between WFOE and the Chinese parent, if any, is includable and subject to interest WHT on distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 12 – Loss Deduction (早年核定虧損扣除)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of the net operating loss computed and assessed by the tax authority in previous years; utilization only within the 10-year statutory carryforward period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The loss carryforward is denied if there was a change of business, change of ownership of more than 50% during the period, or a cessation such that the economic identity is no longer the same; related to the WFOE's capital contribution by the Chinese holding shareholder.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual income after the loss deduction and all statutory exclusions. This is the basis for the 20% corporate income tax computation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Taiwan-source income of a full taxpayer; no branch-return mechanics apply to a Taiwan-incorporated WFOE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Lines 14-17 – Tax Computation (應納稅額計算)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Line 14 calculates tax at 20%; line 15 subtracts investment tax credits; line 16 subtracts foreign income tax credits on Taiwan-assessed foreign-source income; line 17 reports the final self-assessed tax due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credit must be net of specific-country attribution and is unavailable for passive offshore shell income of affiliates. Any credits claimed require certified tax payment evidence from the foreign jurisdiction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Related-Party Disclosure Schedule (附冊四: 關係人及關係人交易明細表)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory schedule listing all related parties, relationship type, transaction types (intangibles, financing, tangible goods), prices charged, and the selected TP method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Chinese parent (CN_WFOE_LTD shareholder) is a related party under Article 43-1 regardless of the absence of a Taiwan–PRC tax treaty; full disclosure of intercompany sales of keycaps is obligatory.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Time-of-filing violations trigger: (1) late filing surcharge of 10% of the assessed tax (underpayment surcharge, 滯報金), predictable under Article 108; (2) failure to file after NTB notice imposes a 20% surcharge (怠報金); (3) late payment accrues 1% interest surcharge per 3 days after the statutory due date, generally capped at 15% aggregate; (4) any willful omission or incorrect declaration invites the Article 110 two-to-three-fold additional tax in lieu of the base tax, and criminal prosecution under Article 41 of the Tax Collection Act.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 15-A – Provisional Tax Return (營利事業所得稅暫繳申報書) filed on the same electronic tax filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year beginning 1 January, filed from 1 September to 30 September; the prepayment equals 50% of the tax assessed on the previous year, with adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The enterprise's estimated taxable income for the interim period; for the WFOE, typically one-half of the prior-year taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An alternative to standard provisional payments is not available for newly commercialized entities without a precedent-year assessment; the firm must make advance payment or pay the difference with penalty interest at finalization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculated provisional tax after the application of available credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Investment tax credits can be applied only at finalization unless a specific provisional credit pre-approval is obtained.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Underpayment of the provisional installment attracts interest calculated at the postal savings one-year fixed rate from the payable date to the final return date; repeated underpayment can trigger a 1% monthly surcharge and tax avoidance audit.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% on gross dividends distributed by the Taiwan WFOE to its non-resident corporate shareholders, applicable under Article 88 and Tax Collection Act enforcement guidelines (rate effective since 2018).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Taiwan maintains only a narrow DTA network (notably with Singapore, Indonesia, New Zealand, Australia, and several other states). There is no implemented Taiwan–PRC comprehensive income tax agreement; the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement, although signed in 2015, lacks Taiwanese ratification and is inapplicable. For treaty-eligible shareholders (e.g., Singapore), protocol requires: (a) the foreign shareholder to be the beneficial owner and produce a current Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from its home tax authority; (b) submission of the 'Application for Application of the Income Tax Agreement' and Form of WHT reduction to the NTB office of jurisdiction before the dividend distribution; (c) the Taiwan WFOE to provide the distribution resolution and audited/un-audited financial statements identifying the profits earmarked for distribution; (d) the NTB grants a certificate-in-principle allowing a reduced rate (most treaties 5–10% on dividends where the shareholder owns at least 25% capital and meets substance tests; otherwise 10–15%); distributions already withheld at 21% may be reclaimed by filing a refund application within five years with a conclusive TRC, documentary evidence of final beneficial ownership, and a statement by the Taiwan company that the withholding was over-deducted.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT for royalties paid to a non-resident: 0%? Incorrect — statutory WHT is 20% on royalties under Article 88. Statutory WHT on interest paid to non-resident corporations: 20%; certain interest paid to foreign financial institutions with an ROC branch is 15%. Relevant DTA negotiated rates generally reduce royalties to 5–10% and interest to 5–10% depending on the jurisdiction, granted strictly via the same pre-approval/TRC process. Because the parent is PRC-based, no treaty relief is available; the WFOE's payments of brand licences or financing interest to the Chinese group suffer full 20% WHT and the payor has a statutory obligation to withhold on the gross amount.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File (移轉訂價文據—「移轉訂價報告」) where the WFOE's related-party transaction amount in a fiscal year reaches NT$200 million (aggregate controlled transactions); the Master File (集團主檔報告) is required when the multinational group's combined global turnover exceeds NT$5 billion and cross-border controlled transactions exceed NT$500 million. Below the NT$200 million threshold, the taxpayer must still provide a related-party disclosure schedule and contemporaneous substantiation upon audit.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Other recognized OECD-aligned methods permissible under administrative guidance
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan does not apply the offshore Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) as codified in the UAE/Cayman framework. However, Taiwan's Income Tax Act contains equivalent substance-over-form doctrine: (i) General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) under Article 43-1 and recognized judicial substance requirements permit the NTB to re-characterize or ignore a transaction arranged without a bona fide commercial purpose; (ii) the CFC regime (Art. 43-3) and Place of Effective Management (PEM) rules (Art. 43-4) attribute offshore income of a controlled foreign corporation to the Taiwan shareholder. For a WFOE in the custom keycap manufacturing sector, the doctrine requires physical manufacturing activity, local payroll (injection moulding operators), inventory risk, intellectual-property substance (ownership or licensed use of double-shot moulding tech), and an actual decision-making office in Taiwan. A WFOE merely outsourcing production to a PRC contract manufacturer to strip profit without operational substance will be re-characterized and its income attributed to Taiwan.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing fictitious electronic VAT uniform invoices (統一發票, including zero-rated export e-invoices) for transactions that did not occur, inflating input tax credits, underestimating revenue from Shopify/Stripe settlements, or repurposing other enterprises' invoicing mirror to simulate third-party sales of keycap manufacturing capacity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Tax Collection Act Art. 41, perjury or fraudulent means to evade income tax are punishable with imprisonment of up to five years, detention, and/or a fine up to NT$6 million; income tax additionally assessed and a surcharge of two to three times the underpaid tax under Income Tax Act Art. 110. For electronic invoice violations, the Unified Invoice penalty ranges between NT$15,000 and NT$1,500,000 per instance together with loss of the invoice-printing licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Management and the sole shareholder of the WFOE are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax arrears after lawful final assessment. Directors can be personally named in the NTB collection summons; travel bans under Tax Collection Act Art. 24 (restriction of departure when arrears exceed NT$1 million) are imposed personally on the responsible director/controller. Fraud participants, including the accountant who designed the false invoicing, face the same criminal exposure under Art. 41.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing / Unjustified Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling double-shot PBT keycaps to the Chinese parent at a Victorian markup yielding a gross margin below the full-cost-plus benchmark (e.g., under 5–8% TNMM margin), renting intangibles to the parent at nil or token rates, or making non-arm's-length year-end retroactive price adjustments to remit profits out of Taiwan without supporting TP documentation, benchmarks, or accurate attribution of moulding R&D earnings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the TP Regulations and Income Tax Act Art. 43-1, the NTB re-computes the arm's-length consideration, increases taxable income, and imposes a surcharge of between 100% and 200% of the incremental tax (Article 110 regime). Failure to timely submit contemporaneous Local/Master File documentation triggers administrative fines of NT$3,000 to NT$300,000 per return and disallowance of the company's intercompany deductions; interest on underpayment is additionally assessed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The chief executive and finance director are treated as responsible collectors; when the increase arises from deliberate dishonest price-setting, criminal liability under Tax Collection Act Art. 41 attaches personally. The NTB may freeze the Taiwanese bank accounts of the directors where the company's main operating receivables have been diverted abroad, and the court may order preservative seizure of personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Taiwan WFOE as a letterbox entity with no injection machinery, no local staffing, no decision-making or keycap moulding records, and with all manufacturing actually executed in China while the WFOE books gross revenue and remits most profits abroad strictly to exploit the 20% headline rate and payment rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Re-characterization of the WFOE under the GAAR (Art. 43-1): the agency/PE structure is disregarded; the Chinese parent is directly assessed on Taiwan-source revenue, resulting in back taxes plus a 1.5- to 2-fold surcharge. The corporate registration authority may initiate company dissolution procedures for inactive or sham enterprises; the business registration can be revoked, affecting VAT zero-rating entitlements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where the sham enterprise results in underpaid corporate tax, directors become jointly and severally liable for the full tax arrears. When the shell is used to move funds to a non-transparent foreign account structure, the responsible director also faces Anti-Money-Laundering Act prosecution for money laundering (up to seven years' imprisonment) and a personal civil restitution claim by the tax authority as creditor.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing Shopify/Stripe proceeds from global keycap sales directly into accounts of the Chinese parent or into personal overseas accounts while classifying the revenue as 'site optimization fees'; or systematically undervaluing export customs declarations to match artificially low transfer prices, without reporting the true FX inflows to the Central Bank; a WFOE receiving US-dollar payments through facilitated rails but never performing a Taiwan foreign-exchange declaration or incurring unreconciled platform payouts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violations of the Foreign Exchange Control Act and the Central Bank declaration rules attract fines of NT$3 million to NT$30 million per unreported inflow, plus the seizure of undeclared funds; falsified customs declarations in the export of keycaps to the parent attract Customs Anti-Smuggling Act penalties of a fine of up to 3x evaded foreign-currency earnings and criminal sanctions of up to one year. The under-declared profit is additionally taxed as unreported revenue at 20% with a 100–200% penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who open offshore collection accounts to receive e-commerce sales—without booking the revenue in the WFOE—convert corporate income into personal wealth; this exposes them to self-dealing/breach of fiduciary claims and to criminal fraudulent concealment. Travel bans, asset-preservation orders on personal bank accounts, and up to five years' imprisonment are available to the tax and money-laundering enforcement authorities; the shareholders of a WFOE can also lose the limited liability shield because the abuse constitutes fraud or gross misconduct under Taiwanese company law.
